name: Honey Mesquite

facts.what: Whole dry pods (not the seeds alone)
facts.how: Grind dry pods into sweet flour; simmer for syrup
facts.value: Natural sugars, protein, fiber; gluten-free flour

caution: Harvest pods straight off the tree, dry and unblemished; ground-collected pods mold fast, and moldy pods are unsafe. Taste one first, sweetness varies tree to tree.

sections.title: Harvesting
sections.body: Pick straw-colored pods that snap cleanly, from the branch rather than the dirt. Dry them brittle in a low oven or a hot truck dashboard, which is the traditional West Texas dehydrator.

sections.title: Mesquite flour
sections.body: Blitz brittle pods, sift, repeat. The flour is sweet with a cocoa-coffee edge and swaps for a quarter of the flour in pancakes and cornbread.
